De C.V., v. United States, Slip Op. 26-128, Consol. Court no. 25-00235, sustaining the U.S. Department of Commerce's (Commerce) first remand redetermination pertaining to the less-than-fair-value (LTFV) investigation of corrosion-resistant steel products (CORE) from Mexico covering the period of investigation July 1, 2023, through June 30, 2024. Commerce is notifying the public that the CIT's final judgment is not in harmony with Commerce's final determination in that investigation, and that Commerce is amending the final determination and the resulting AD order with respect to the dumping margin assigned to Galvasid S.A. De C.V. its continuing effort to reduce paperwork burdens, and as required by the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) of 1995, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) invites the general public and other Federal agencies to take this opportunity to comment on the following information collection. Comments are requested concerning: whether the collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the Commission, including whether the information shall have practical utility; the accuracy of the Commission's burden estimate; ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information collected; ways to minimize the burden of the collection of information on the respondents, including the use of automated collection techniques or other forms of information technology; and ways to further reduce the information collection burden on small business concerns with fewer than 25 employees.","publishedAt":"2026-11-02","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22337","title":"Unleashing the Power of Unlicensed Ultra-Wideband Devices; Petition of Robert Bosch LLC for Amendment of the Part 15 Subpart F Ultra-Wideband Rules; and Petition of Alliance for Automative Innovation et al. To Amend Part 15 of the FCC's Rules To Permit the Operation of Certain Ultra-Wideband Devices","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/02/2026-22337/unleashing-the-power-of-unlicensed-ultra-wideband-devices-petition-of-robert-bosch-llc-for-amendment","summary":"The Federal Communications Commission (Commission or FCC) proposes to update its rules for Ultra-Wideband (UWB) devices to reflect significant technological developments since the rules were first adopted in 2002. UWB technology has matured into a widely used, low-power enabler that supports applications in tracking, automation, precision location, health monitoring, athletic performance, and public safety. As capabilities of UWB have expanded, the existing rules have not kept pace with the technological change, resulting in an increasing number of waiver requests received by the Commission to authorize modern devices. The Notice of Proposed Rulemaking seeks comment on revisions intended to modernize the UWB framework, provide greater flexibility for future applications, promote continued innovation, and ensure the protection of incumbent federal and non-federal spectrum users.","publishedAt":"2026-11-02","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22336","title":"Notice of Petition for Waiver of Compliance","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/02/2026-22336/notice-of-petition-for-waiver-of-compliance","summary":"This document extends the period for public comment regarding the CSX Transportation Inc.
